subject: How to do the BMA using inla for a beta regression and binomial regression

messages.author: 7c80fc81c3454752
messages.subject: How to do the BMA using inla for a beta regression and binomial regression
parts:
Hi,

I want to do a model averaging for estimating the proportions. 

One candidate is the beta regression and another is the binomial regression.

Both of them have some bad performance on observation cases.

I do notice the V. Gómez-Rubio, R. S. Bivand and H. Rue (2019). Bayesian model averaging with the integrated nested Laplace approximation. 

But I'm still not sure how to do BMA in my case, as the hyperparameters are different in my 2 models.

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to do the BMA using inla for a beta regression and binomial regression
parts: you can weight them using the marginal likelihood, if you use proper priors
